app_info.subtitle: Check plots for deforestation and prepare the EU filing
app_info.description: Check agricultural plots for forest loss after the EU Deforestation Regulation's 31 December 2020 cut-off, find what an Article 9 supplier file is missing, and compile a signed Annex II Due Diligence Statement. Every verdict is measured per satellite cell rather than estimated from an area average, and every statement carries two independent signatures — ours over the document and emem.dev's over the satellite measurement — so a buyer or an auditor can verify it offline without trusting either of us. It answers Article 3(a), deforestation-free, and says on every response which checks it did not perform: land tenure, permits and free, prior and informed consent are documentary questions that satellites cannot answer.

justifications.read_only_justification: Measures land and returns a verdict, and nothing about the caller's account or records changes — but it is not a read. Each call asks emem.dev for freshly signed measurements and mints a short-lived evidence handle in this server's process store, so running it twice does not leave the state running it once leaves: the second call returns the same finding under new signatures at a new address, and the first call's handle is not the one it resolves. Marked neither read-only nor idempotent for that reason.
justifications.open_world_justification: Sends plot geometry, commodity, country and quantity to emem.dev, an independent Earth-observation service, which measures the land and signs the result. Operator and supplier identity are never forwarded.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten. A check that finds forest loss reports it; it does not alter the plot, the account, the wallet or any previous check. The evidence handle it mints is new each time rather than a replacement for an existing one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Pages through satellite facts already fetched and addressed by a previous check. It reads a stored set and returns a slice of it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads facts held on eudr.dev against a content address minted earlier. It reaches no third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reads only; the evidence set is immutable.

justifications.read_only_justification: Compares supplier details the caller supplies against the Article 9(1) checklist and returns what is missing. Nothing is stored.
justifications.open_world_justification: Pure evaluation against the regulation's closed list of seven items. No network call leaves the process.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns country risk tiers from Implementing Regulation 2025/1093 and the Annex I commodity mapping. A lookup against bundled reference data.
justifications.open_world_justification: The reference tables ship with the service. No external call.

justifications.read_only_justification: Checks an ed25519 signature and a content address against a receipt the caller supplies. A verification, not a mutation.
justifications.open_world_justification: Verification is arithmetic over the receipt's own bytes and a public key. It deliberately requires no network call, so a holder can check a statement without trusting or reaching eudr.dev.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes: it stores a compile task holding the operator and supplier details supplied, produces a signed statement, and spends 5 credits from the organisation's wallet.
justifications.open_world_justification: Sends plot geometry, HS code, country of production and quantity to emem.dev to be measured and independently signed. Operator and supplier identity are not forwarded. Nothing is filed with any authority: filing to TRACES NT is a separate, explicit operator action that is not on this surface.
justifications.destructive_justification: Marked destructive because a successful compile spends five credits from the organisation's wallet, and spending that stands is not undoable by the caller. A compile that fails refunds them automatically. Nothing is deleted: it creates a new statement and never modifies or removes an earlier one, because a filed statement must stay reconstructable.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads the outcome of a compile the caller already started.
Returns the ordered derivation chain behind a verdict — which stage produced what, and which stages did not run and why.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads a trace already recorded locally.

justifications.read_only_justification: Parses a CSV or GS1 EPCIS consignment list the caller supplies and returns the structured result for review. It does not persist the rows or start a compile — importing and committing are deliberately separate, so a mis-parsed file is caught before it becomes a record.
justifications.open_world_justification: Parsing happens in-process; no external call.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is stored, so nothing can be overwritten.

justifications.read_only_justification: Renders a statement the organisation already holds as TRACES NT XML, Annex II JSON or plot GeoJSON.
justifications.open_world_justification: Formats stored data. Producing the TRACES XML does not transmit it — submission to the EU Information System is a separate operator action, off this surface.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists statements the organisation has compiled.
Summarises the organisation's statements by verdict and outstanding obligation.
Lists evidence requests the organisation has issued and whether each was answered.
Writes: it mints a shareable link that lets a named supplier submit plot data into this organisation. That link is a credential, which is why this is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: Creates the link and stores it. Delivering it to the supplier is the operator's own act — this tool does not send email or reach any third party.
justifications.destructive_justification: Additive. A new request never revokes or overwrites an existing one, and the link carries no read access to anything the organisation already holds.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports the organisation's credit balance and what it covers, and on the first call for a given organisation it also opens the wallet, grants the welcome credits and writes that grant as the opening ledger line. That first call is a write, so the tool is not marked read-only. Every call after it only reads, which is why it stays idempotent.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads and, on first use, opens the local wallet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is removed or overwritten; the first-use grant is additive and happens once. It cannot buy credits or spend a balance — purchasing happens on eudr.dev behind a session and is not reachable from any tool.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports which Article 11 mitigation steps are outstanding on a flagged shipment. Recording a decision is a deliberate human act done on eudr.dev, because Article 11(3) requires mitigation decisions to be documented and demonstrable; eudr.dev records each against the named person who made it.
Lists the organisation's farms and its stored buying decisions, with recorded outcomes and overrides. Changes nothing.
Writes: it stores the buying decision it computes, so an outcome can later be recorded against it and each voter scored. It spends no credits and signs nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Runs on this service only: the organisation's own buying process, its destination library and its track records. Nothing leaves eudr.dev.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a decision record; overwrites and deletes nothing.

test_cases.description: Check a single cocoa plot against the EUDR cut-off
test_cases.user_prompt: Check this cocoa plot in Côte d'Ivoire for deforestation since the EUDR cut-off: a polygon around 5.690115, -6.699723.
test_cases.expected_output: A per-plot verdict against the 31 December 2020 cut-off, the loss years actually observed, how much of the polygon was inspected, and a content address for the signed satellite facts behind it. The response also names the checks it did not perform — tenure, permits and consent are documentary and out of scope.

test_cases.description: Page the evidence behind a check
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the satellite facts behind that verdict.
test_cases.expected_output: A page of the individually signed facts the check rested on, each with its own content address, and a count of how many there are in total.

test_cases.description: Find what an Article 9 supplier file is missing
test_cases.user_prompt: I have two coffee suppliers in Ethiopia. One sent plot boundaries for four of four plots plus land-use rights; the other sent three of twelve and nothing else. What am I missing under Article 9?
test_cases.expected_output: The Article 9(1) checklist per supplier, which gaps are blocking rather than advisory, and the article each sits under. The second supplier comes back blocked on geolocation coverage — nine plots with no boundaries is not a file that can be filed on.

test_cases.description: Look up a country's risk tier
test_cases.user_prompt: What risk tier is Côte d'Ivoire under the EUDR country benchmarking, and does simplified due diligence apply?
test_cases.expected_output: The tier from Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1093 with the regulation cited, and whether Article 13 simplified due diligence is available — it is not, above low risk.

test_cases.description: Verify a statement without trusting the sender
test_cases.user_prompt: A supplier sent me a due diligence statement with receipt CID bafkr4iagzkkfm55z33av66q. Is the signature genuine?
test_cases.expected_output: Whether the ed25519 signature checks out against the published key and whether the content address matches the bytes. The response is explicit that this establishes authorship and integrity — who signed it and that it has not been altered — and not that the underlying measurement is correct.

negative_test_cases.description: Refuses to file with an authority
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Submit this statement to TRACES NT for me.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: It declines and explains that nothing here files with any authority. The TRACES XML can be exported for the operator to submit themselves; transmitting a legal filing on someone's behalf is deliberately not on this surface.

negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Buy me 50 more credits so I can keep compiling.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: It declines. No tool can take a payment or change a balance — buying credits happens on eudr.dev behind a signed-in session. It can report the current balance with eudr_account_usage.

negative_test_cases.description: Refuses to call a clean forest check a clean compliance file
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: The plot check came back with no forest loss, so this shipment is EUDR compliant — confirm that for my buyer.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: It declines to confirm. A clean forest-loss result answers Article 3(a) only; Article 3(b) legality — tenure, permits, free prior and informed consent — is documentary and was not checked. It explains the difference rather than agreeing.
